## Proof

We present the abelian group via the relation matrix and compute its Smith normal form.

Let $A = \mathbb{Z}^3 / \langle r_1, r_2, r_3\rangle$ where the relations correspond to the rows of

$$M = \begin{pmatrix} 9 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}.$$

The group $A$ is determined by the Smith normal form of $M$.

**Row/column reduction.**

1. Swap $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 9 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & -3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}$$

2. $R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 3R_1$, $\;R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - R_1$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \end{pmatrix}$$

3. $C_2 \leftarrow C_2 - C_1$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \end{pmatrix}$$

4. $R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - R_2$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

5. $C_3 \leftarrow C_3 + C_2$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

Taking absolute values, the diagonal is $(3, 6, 0)$, and the divisibility condition $3 \mid 6 \mid 0$ holds. Hence the Smith normal form is

$$\operatorname{diag}(3, 6, 0).$$

**Verification via minors.** The rank is $2$ (indeed $r_1 = r_3 + 2r_2$, so the rows have rank $2$). The first invariant factor $d_1 = \gcd(9,3,6,3,3,0,3,-3,6) = 3$. The product $d_1 d_2 = \gcd$ of all $2\times 2$ minors; the minors are $\pm 18$ and $\pm 36$, with $\gcd = 18 = 3\cdot 6$. Thus $d_2 = 6$, confirming $\operatorname{diag}(3,6,0)$.

**Decomposition.** From the Smith normal form,

$$A \cong \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}.$$

The problem requests cyclic summands of **prime order or infinite order**, so we split $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ (since $\gcd(2,3)=1$):

$$\boxed{A \cong \mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
